methods.label: Factor using the digits
methods.explanation:
Writing the numbers in terms of their digits makes the reversal condition easy to use. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be the tens and ones digits of \(x\), respectively. Since both numbers have two digits,
\[
x=10a+b,\qquad y=10b+a,\qquad 1\le a,b\le9.
\]
Because \(m>0\), we have \(x^2>y^2\). Both numbers are positive, so \(x>y\), which means \(a>b\).

Factoring the difference of squares gives
\[
m^2=(x-y)(x+y)=99(a-b)(a+b).
\]
Every prime factor of a perfect square occurs an even number of times. Since \(99=3^2\cdot11\) supplies one factor of \(11\), the product \((a-b)(a+b)\) must supply another. But \(1\le a-b\le8\), so \(a-b\) is not divisible by \(11\). As \(11\) is prime, \(a+b\) must be divisible by \(11\). The digit bounds give \(3\le a+b\le17\), so
\[
a+b=11.
\]
Substituting this back gives
\[
m^2=33^2(a-b).
\]
Thus \(33\) divides \(m\), and \(a-b=(m/33)^2\) is an integer square. Also, \(a+b\) is odd, so one digit is odd and the other is even; hence \(a-b\) is odd. The only odd square from \(1\) through \(8\) is \(1\). Therefore \(a-b=1\).

The equations \(a+b=11\) and \(a-b=1\) give \(a=6\) and \(b=5\). Hence \(x=65\), \(y=56\), and \(m=33\). These values satisfy the original condition because
\[
65^2-56^2=9\cdot121=33^2.
\]
Therefore \(x+y+m=65+56+33=\boxed{154}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
